D.basis: Conversion is included but is not the focus.

F.basis: NetX is named without comparative analysis.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Combines a broad tutorial with controlled neuron, code, framework, and proxy-energy experiments.
surveys.deployment_depth: Software experiments only; no physical neuromorphic deployment is reported.
omissions: Energy is an operation-count proxy rather than instrumented chip energy.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Provides a compact comparison of representative neuromorphic architecture families.
surveys.deployment_depth: Descriptive hardware comparison without a traced model-to-chip route.
omissions: Software handoffs and measurement boundaries are not systematized.

B.basis: Event sampling and AER are central, but no broad neural-code taxonomy is provided.

G.basis: AER is sensor protocol, not model interchange.

H.basis: Visual, auditory, and olfactory sensing systems are reviewed.

K.basis: Applications are synthesized across three modalities.

L.basis: No trained SNN to chip route.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Unifies event-based visual, auditory, and olfactory sensing principles.
surveys.deployment_depth: Covers sensor systems rather than trained SNN deployment toolchains.
omissions: Sensor address-event representation is not a model interchange format.

B.basis: Event packet and AER representations are explained.

G.basis: AER is not treated as general interchange.

H.basis: Sensor generations and hardware are reviewed.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Connects neuromorphic vision sensor hardware with algorithms and applications.
surveys.deployment_depth: Focuses on sensing rather than compute-chip execution routes.
omissions: No general compiler, mapper, or executable-semantics taxonomy is provided.

A.basis: Target is directly trained LIF SNNs.

C.basis: Direct training and surrogate difficulty are analyzed.

I.basis: Reset is within-neuron, not boundary semantics.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Organizes SNN development as a four-stage structural evolution from binary ANNs.
surveys.deployment_depth: Algorithmic perspective with no named physical deployment route.
omissions: The review deliberately narrows its treatment of codes, platforms, and applications.

A.basis: Develops a taxonomy from biophysical models through IF-family, phenomenological, dendritic, astrocyte-modulated, and synaptic models.

B.basis: Compares direct, rate, temporal, TTFS, phase, bit-plane, burst, and event-sensor encodings with equations and limitations.

C.basis: Covers temporal backpropagation, surrogate gradients, online alternatives, STDP variants, supervised local learning, reward modulation, and hybrid training.

D.basis: Explains threshold balancing, batch-normalization absorption, pooling and residual compatibility, conversion latency, low-timestep techniques, and transformer conversion.

E.basis: Compares 20 open-source SNN frameworks by training paradigm, interface, purpose, maintenance, and documentation.

F.basis: Discusses depth-wise and spatial mapping, workload balancing, placement, and hardware constraints without comparing concrete compiler toolchains.

G.basis: No interchange-format treatment was found; NIR is cited only as support for graph-structured SNN foundations.

H.basis: Surveys digital, analog, mixed-signal, memristive, photonic, and quantum-inspired substrates and compares representative platforms.

I.basis: Discusses discretization, parameter approximations, quantization, mapping, payload, reset, memory, and learning-state costs without a cross-boundary semantic taxonomy.

J.basis: No classification separates physical measurement, modeled hardware, operation-count proxies, and software simulation.

K.basis: Covers computer vision, graphs, language, reinforcement learning, sensing, hybrid systems, hardware, and emerging models with reported results.

L.basis: No worked route follows one trained network through export, compilation, mapping, physical execution, and measurement on a named chip.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Provides unusually broad field-entry coverage from neuron dynamics through applications, hardware, and software frameworks.
surveys.deployment_depth: Explains hardware-aware design and mapping conceptually, but does not trace an exercised model-to-chip route.
omissions: No literature-wide evidence taxonomy or end-to-end physical deployment case is provided.

A.basis: LIF dynamics, reset, and refractoriness are explained.

B.basis: Spike timing is discussed without coding taxonomy.

C.basis: Training taxonomy spans key learning classes.

E.basis: One open snnTorch benchmarking framework is defined, without a comparative framework survey.

I.basis: Learning locality is not deployment-boundary semantics.

J.basis: Controlled benchmarking is emphasized without evidence classes.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Pairs a local-learning taxonomy with an open snnTorch benchmarking framework.
surveys.deployment_depth: Benchmarking is software-based and does not establish a named physical route.
omissions: Compiler, interchange, and cross-platform execution semantics remain outside scope.

A.basis: Implements and compares 13 neuron models while controlling topology and training, including differences in leakage, threshold, reset, and adaptation.

B.basis: Compares direct, rate, TTFS, phase, burst, and temporal-switch encodings across modalities and identifies direct input as non-spike-compatible.

C.basis: Uses surrogate-gradient backpropagation and supports 13 surrogate formulations without surveying the broader direct-training landscape.

D.basis: No ANN-to-SNN conversion method or conversion-error analysis is presented.

E.basis: Specifies Soul-NeuSim and compares it with selected SNN software and simulators without systematically reviewing the wider framework landscape.

F.basis: Provides synapse extraction, operator fusion, capacity-constrained partitioning, logical-core clustering, mesh placement, and simulator execution.

G.basis: No hardware-neutral SNN interchange format or NIR-like semantic contract is described.

H.basis: Evaluates seven named physical edge devices and models Loihi, Darwin3, TrueNorth, and SpiNNaker2.
H.locator: Results, pages 6-7, Methods, pages 12-14, and Figure 4, page 22

I.basis: Exposes representation and execution boundaries involving spike compatibility, backend support, temporal state, recurrent latency, memory, and hardware dependence.

J.basis: Separates physical device profiling from cycle-level neuromorphic simulation and defines system metrics, but does not classify evidence across the literature.
J.locator: Results, pages 6-7, Methods, pages 11-14, and Figure 4, page 22

K.basis: Reports repeated, matched experiments across vision, acoustic, motion, wireless, and neuromorphic event sensing.
K.locator: Results, pages 3-8, Table 1, page 20, and Methods, page 10

L.basis: Routes trained models through NCNN to seven physical edge devices and through a complete NeuSim mapper, while named neuromorphic chips remain simulated.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Tests when SNNs benefit edge sensing across modalities, model choices, physical devices, and modeled neuromorphic platforms.
surveys.deployment_depth: Measures seven conventional edge devices and describes a complete NeuSim mapping route, while named neuromorphic chips remain simulated.
omissions: The supplied PDF omits the supplement containing detailed device settings and additional metric procedures.

A.basis: LIF and Izhikevich are introduced, not broadly surveyed.

B.basis: Rate, temporal, population, and phase codes are identified.

C.basis: STDP, surrogate gradients, and conversion are identified.

E.basis: GPU ecosystems and simulation frameworks are cataloged.

F.basis: GPU and RISC-V accelerator and toolchain taxonomy.

H.basis: GPU and RISC-V accelerators are surveyed extensively, but neuromorphic hardware platforms are not surveyed comprehensively.

I.basis: Cross-platform constraints are analyzed without semantic-preservation taxonomy.

L.basis: Edge deployment is a taxonomy category, without a standard route.

surveys.strongest_contribution: Provides a GPU and RISC-V accelerator taxonomy and identifies incompatible reporting practices.
surveys.deployment_depth: Synthesizes accelerator studies but does not trace a standard network across complete routes.
omissions: The accepted manuscript is not yet the final version of record.
